positioning.brief_for_strategy:
4 competitor(s) read - open ground on security.

**Open ground - lead here.** Nothing else in this list differentiates this company, and a claim nobody else makes is worth more than a stronger claim everybody makes:
- **security** - Cal.com's product is ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, CCPA, and GDPR compliant; Cal.com offers multiple payment options including credit card and bank transfer, and absorbs the associated fees (nobody else claims it).

**Contested - usable, but the reader has heard it.** Argue these, never assert them:
- **proof** - Flo Merian, Product Marketing at Mintlify, said Cal.com is more elegant than Calendly, more open than SavvyCal, and works and feels just right; Guillermo Rauch, CEO of Vercel, said he thinks Cal.com has a very good chance of creating a new category around being both great and well designed.; Aria Minaei, CEO of Theatre.JS, said it's definitely the easiest meeting she's ever scheduled.; Ant Wilson, Co-Founder & CTO of Supabase, said he finally made the move to Cal.com after he couldn't find how to edit events in the Calendly dashboard.; Micah Friedland, CEO & Founder of Navi, said that at Navi, protecting personal health information is a non-negotiable, so choosing Cal.com for scheduling just makes sense.; Flo Merian, Product Marketing at Mintlify, is a named Cal.com customer/user; Kent C. Dodds, Founder of EpicWeb.dev, said he just migrated from Calendly to Cal.com.; Supabase is a customer of Cal.com, represented by Ant Wilson, Co-Founder & CTO.; Navi is a customer of Cal.com, represented by Micah Friedland, CEO & Founder.; Vercel is a customer of Cal.com, represented by Guillermo Rauch, CEO.; Theatre.JS is a customer of Cal.com, represented by Aria Minaei, CEO. (1 competitor(s) also claim it).

**Table stakes - true, and worth nothing as an argument.** Every competitor says these. An email that leads on one of them is an email the reader has already received:
- **speed** - Cal.com's buffer time setting ensures 5 to 10 minutes between meetings.; CalVideo meetings don't automatically end or time out after 45 minutes and can be as long or short as needed; Time-slot intervals control which time increments are available for bookings, e.g. event length or every 15, 30, or 60 minutes (4 competitor(s) also claim it).
- **price** - Free Cal.com users have access to over 90% of all the platform's features; The Teams plan costs $12 per user/month billed yearly; Upgrading to a premium username costs $29 a month; A team account costs $15 per month per team member; Individual accounts on Cal.com are free; All subscription tiers except the free tier support CalVideo recording (3 competitor(s) also claim it).
- **breadth** - Cal.com integrates with Zoom to host meetings, but meetings longer than 45 minutes require a paid Zoom account.; Cal.com integrates with Stripe and PayPal for booking payments. (4 competitor(s) also claim it).
- **support** - The Teams plan comes with a 14 day free trial; Users cannot rebrand and republish the enterprise edition (/ee/) of Cal.com without purchasing a license and permission (2 competitor(s) also claim it).
- **other** - As of 15th December 2025, Cal.com no longer offers new signups for any Platform plan, though it continues to provide enterprise support for existing Platform customers.; Removing Cal.com's branding from the booking interface requires signing up for a team plan, which can consist of a single individual; Cal.com branding can be removed from booking pages by upgrading to a Teams level account; Multiple duration options let a company offer different meeting lengths for the same event type, e.g. 15, 30, or 60 mins (3 competitor(s) also claim it).

**Where the field is ahead of us.** Do not raise these:
- **quality** - Calendly, SavvyCal, Chili Piper, Microsoft Bookings claim this and we do not. Do not invite the comparison: an email that raises this axis loses on it.
- **effort** - Calendly, SavvyCal, Chili Piper, Microsoft Bookings claim this and we do not. Do not invite the comparison: an email that raises this axis loses on it.
- **control** - SavvyCal claim this and we do not. Do not invite the comparison: an email that raises this axis loses on it.

**The category's own words.** Two or more competitors spend these. A sentence built only out of them says nothing about this company:
- booking, meeting, meetings, schedule, scheduling, based, book, email, join, link, reminders, time, access, account, app, assign, assistant, availability, available, behalf, booked, bookings, built-in, calendar
